title: Value embeddings on every layer (has_ve -> True)
description: One line: has_ve() returns True, so all 10 layers get a value-residual embedding + gate instead of 5; params 85.9M -> 112.1M, FLOPs/token unchanged.
reflection: NEGATIVE, small: val_bpb 0.983208 vs the 0.981817 baseline, +0.0014 (~1.7 sigma on the round-4 arm-to-arm sd of 8e-4). 1145 steps, 300.2M tokens (baseline 1168 / 306.2M, -2.0%), MFU 40.17% (41.00%), peak VRAM 69.6GB (66.2GB), 112.1M params, 300.2s. Mean-last-60 train loss 2.7577 vs the baseline's 2.758 - identical. So the honest split is: the +26M FLOP-free embedding params cost ~2% of tokens (gathers plus backward scatter-adds are memory-bound, not free as the FLOP count implies) which is worth ~+0.001 by this cell's token calibration, leaving a representational term of roughly zero. Doubling value-embedding coverage buys nothing. This matches a5's dim-512 tie from round 2: capacity is simply not the binding constraint at this horizon, and 'FLOP-free capacity' is not free either - estimate_flops excludes embeddings, but the HBM traffic and the Adam updates are real wall-clock. VRAM prediction (69-72GB) was accurate. The alternating VE pattern inherited from modded-nanogpt is at or near its optimum here, so with a4 probing the sparse direction the VE axis should be closed after this round unless a4 finds a win.
